parsed.explanation: The combined regime is dominated by national document and custody rules. A trans visitor whose presentation and documents diverge can be refused a visa or entry, flagged, and face a possible permanent misrepresentation finding; reports describe confiscated passports and stranded travellers. National policy bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity, and immigration/corrections custody carries documented abuse and denial of care. The division adds a school-only facility ban, a minors' care ban, a hate-crime statute that omits gender identity, and no statewide public-accommodations protection, but no adult bathroom rule. National hate-crime coverage and pending litigation are partial remedies, not operative protections at the border. Social climate is divided and no trans-specific violence rate is documented. For an adult alone, border and facility exposure dominate; for an adult with a trans minor, care and school exclusion add material harm. Elevated Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: National rules require sex assigned at birth on passports/visas, stop X markers, and direct refusal where documents or records cast doubt on sex; misrepresentation can support permanent ineligibility. Travellers report confiscated or blocked passports.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; litigation is pending; a legal-aid FAQ explains document options. No documented working border remedy for a flagged visitor.
entry_documents.interaction: A home passport or visa showing a marker different from presentation can trigger secondary screening, refusal, or detention; the division has no separate entry rule.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of trans men; national corrections policies impose conversion-therapy-style measures, deny hormones, and stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No operative visitor-facing safeguard in custody is described.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A border document discrepancy can move a traveller into immigration detention, where placement and treatment are by birth sex and abuse is documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. Division law restricts transgender public-school students to birth-sex facilities; no adult statewide bathroom rule is identified. Four states criminalise some bathroom use; one arrest.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division facility provision is written for public-school students and left to district guidance; it does not reach adult visitors. National order has no documented visitor exemption.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Adult visitors face national facility exclusion in federal settings; a trans minor in a school context faces the division ban; criminal trespass risk is state-specific and not documented here.

care_services.exposure: Division bans puberty blockers and hormones for minors with no phase-out; national policy targets minors' gender-affirming care, subpoenas hospital records, and proposes insurance bars. Adult visitor care access is not documented.
care_services.protection: Division bars conversion therapy on minors; litigation continues. No documented protection for a visiting minor seeking care or for adult HRT import/refill.
care_services.interaction: A travelling family with a trans minor cannot obtain care in the division; an adult's emergency or routine care exposure is uncertain.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups among priorities; DOJ reward guidance and executive orders frame gender ideology as extremist or abusive, and direct prosecution of teachers aiding social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy says counterterrorism will not target mere disagreement; several orders are enjoined. No visitor-specific protection is documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Ordinary tourists are unlikely targets, but visible activism, medication, or document flags could draw official scrutiny.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minors face the division care ban, school facility restriction, and school-sports ban; national orders frame care as mutilation, subpoena under-19 records, and threaten teachers. A parent seeking care may face investigation.
minors_guardians.protection: Division conversion-therapy ban and pending care-ban litigation; no phase-out or visitor exception. No documented protection for a trans minor travelling through.
minors_guardians.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor faces care denial and school/sports exclusion; border document checks add outing risk for the minor.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division hate-crime statute omits gender identity, so bias violence gets no state enhancement; no statewide public-accommodations law; 2025 polling shows majority support for birth-sex document rules. No trans-specific violence rate is documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 19 municipalities have local ordinances; a 2011 sexual-orientation case produced arrests and pleas. Enforcement for trans visitors is undocumented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: If a visitor is attacked, state hate-crime recourse is absent and national coverage may apply; local ordinances cover only 19 municipalities.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No documented working remedy for border refusal, facility exclusion, or custody abuse; litigation over passports and executive orders is unresolved; division lacks statewide accommodations protection.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National civil-liberties suit, injunctions blocking some orders, legal-aid FAQ, and national hate-crime statute exist; none is shown operative for a flagged visitor at the border.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are slow and prospective; a visitor must navigate entry and custody before any court relief, and standing/access are uncertain.

anchor_checks.comparison: This anchor has a statutory bar on detention for document mismatch, so the worst outcome is invasive review and denial of entry. Our case lacks that bar: national cable allows refusal and a possible permanent fraud finding, and detention can lead to documented custody abuse. Our rating is lower.

This anchor involves a registry cross-check, denied boarding and no formal detention. Our case adds national document rules that can bar entry or visa issuance, a possible lifetime ineligibility finding, facility exclusion, and severe custody risk. It is materially worse.

This anchor has a formal protection that mostly works, with public scrutiny and delay. Our case has no documented working border or facility remedy; national policy itself creates the exposure. It is far below.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is national-first. Entry screening and visa/document rules can out a trans visitor, refuse entry, or start a permanent misrepresentation finding; national facility policy excludes trans people from congruent single-sex government facilities; and immigration/corrections custody carries documented abuse. The division sharpens the picture for minors and recourse: it bans care for trans minors, restricts school facilities, excludes gender identity from hate-crime law, and lacks statewide accommodations protection, though it has no adult bathroom rule. National hate-crime coverage, litigation and injunctions are partial, not working visitor protections. Social climate is contested but no organized street targeting or trans-specific violence rate is documented. An adult alone faces border and facility risk; an adult with a trans minor faces added care and school exclusion. The combined regime sits in Elevated Risk.
